From 932ac51d9953eaf77a1252f79b656d4ca86163c6 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jiri Pirko <jiri@nvidia.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Dec 2025 11:29:53 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] team: fix check for port enabled in
 team_queue_override_port_prio_changed()

There has been a syzkaller bug reported recently with the following
trace:

list_del corruption, ffff888058bea080->prev is LIST_POISON2 (dead000000000122)

diff --git a/drivers/net/team/team_core.c b/drivers/net/team/team_core.c
index 4d5c9ae8f221..c08a5c1bd6e4 100644
--- a/drivers/net/team/team_core.c
+++ b/drivers/net/team/team_core.c
@@ -878,7 +878,7 @@ static void __team_queue_override_enabled_check(struct team *team)
 static void team_queue_override_port_prio_changed(struct team *team,
 						  struct team_port *port)
 {
-	if (!port->queue_id || team_port_enabled(port))
+	if (!port->queue_id || !team_port_enabled(port))
 		return;
 	__team_queue_override_port_del(team, port);
 	__team_queue_override_port_add(team, port);
-- 
2.34.1

The patch fixes a logic error in the `team_queue_override_port_prio_changed()` function in `drivers/net/team/team_core.c`. The change inverts the condition from `team_port_enabled(port)` to `!team_port_enabled(port)`, ensuring that the function correctly returns early when the port is **disabled** (not when it is enabled). This prevents the function from incorrectly attempting to delete and re-add a disabled port to the queue override list, which could lead to list corruption (as reported by syzkaller). The single-line fix resolves the kernel crash by making the early return consistent with the intended behavior: only update the queue override list when the port is enabled and has a valid queue ID.

The problem is in this flow:
1) Port is enabled, queue_id != 0, in qom_list
2) Port gets disabled
        -> team_port_disable()
        -> team_queue_override_port_del()
        -> del (removed from list)
3) Port is disabled, queue_id != 0, not in any list
4) Priority changes
        -> team_queue_override_port_prio_changed()
        -> checks: port disabled && queue_id != 0
        -> calls del - hits the BUG as it is removed already

To fix this, change the check in team_queue_override_port_prio_changed()
so it returns early if port is not enabled.

Reported-by: syzbot+422806e5f4cce722a71f@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Closes: https://syzkaller.appspot.com/bug?extid=422806e5f4cce722a71f
Fixes: 6c31ff366c11 ("team: remove synchronize_rcu() called during queue override change")
Signed-off-by: Jiri Pirko <jiri@nvidia.com>
Reviewed-by: Simon Horman <horms@kernel.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20251212102953.167287-1-jiri@resnulli.us
Signed-off-by: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>

Here is the root cause:
The condition in `team_queue_override_port_prio_changed()` was incorrectly written as `if (!port->queue_id || team_port_enabled(port))` causing the function to return early when the port is enabled, skipping the necessary deletion and re-addition of the port to the queue override list. This leads to list corruption (as reported by syzkaller) because the port's queue override entry is not properly updated when its priority changes. The correct condition should be `if (!port->queue_id || !team_port_enabled(port))` to return early only when the port is disabled or has no queue ID.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void team_queue_override_port_prio_changed(struct team *team,
 						  struct team_port *port)
 {
-	if (!port->queue_id || team_port_enabled(port))
+	if (!port->queue_id || !team_port_enabled(port))
 		return;
 	__team_queue_override_port_del(team, port);
 	__team_queue_override_port_add(team, port);
 	__team_queue_override_enabled_check(team);
 }
